findings.explanation: HOL4's only defining theorem is HD (h::t) = h. It is made by primitive recursion through new_specification (Defn.sml:1192, Prim_rec.sml:281), which says nothing about the omitted [] clause, and I found no saved theorem fixing HD []. Lean's second clause proves HD [] = ARB, and through EL also EL n [] = ARB. Together with LAST it proves HD [] = LAST []. HOL4 leaves HD [] = ARB and HD [] = LAST [] open. SEG, in the same module, uses epsilon over its specification and avoids this.
findings.repair:
def HD_spec {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] (f : List α → α) : Prop := ∀ h t, f (h :: t) = h

def HD {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] : List α → α := Classical.epsilon (HD_spec (α := α))

theorem HD_def {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] : HD_spec (HD (α := α)) := by
  apply Classical.epsilon_spec (p := HD_spec (α := α))
  exact ⟨fun l => match l with | h :: _ => h | [] => Classical.choice ‹Nonempty α›, fun _ _ => rfl⟩
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.Prelude.List

theorem hd_nil {α : Type} [Nonempty α] : HOL.HD ([] : List α) = HOL.ARB := by
  simp [HOL.HD]
findings.hol4_check: ?f:bool list -> bool. (!h t. f (h::t) = h) /\ f [] <> ARB

findings.explanation: HOL4's LAST_DEF has the single clause LAST (h::t) = if t = [] then h else LAST t. It is made by primitive recursion through new_specification with no [] clause. LAST_EL and LAST_MAP require a non-empty list, and I found no saved theorem fixing LAST []. Lean adds the clause LAST [] = ARB, so it proves LAST [] = ARB and also LAST [] = HD [], both of which HOL4 leaves open.
findings.repair:
def LAST_spec {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] (f : List α → α) : Prop :=
  ∀ h t, f (h :: t) = if t = [] then h else f t

def LAST {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] : List α → α := Classical.epsilon (LAST_spec (α := α))

theorem LAST_DEF {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] : LAST_spec (LAST (α := α)) := by
  apply Classical.epsilon_spec (p := LAST_spec (α := α))
  refine ⟨fun l => List.rec (motive := fun _ => α) (Classical.choice ‹Nonempty α›) (fun h t r => if t = [] then h else r) l, ?_⟩
  intro h t
  rfl
